verdictExplanation: The system rejects applicants on its own and scores employee sentiment from workplace messages, which puts it at indicative tier IV. OIPC BC regards continuous, routine employee monitoring as seldom authorized, so the sentiment scoring is a blocker as designed. The redesign path is to drop the continuous sentiment scoring, limit any measurement to a narrow and overt purpose, and keep a person in each hiring decision.

intake.title: Applicant screening and team sentiment scoring
intake.processDescription: Recruiters at a regional logistics company read several hundred applications for each warehouse and driver posting and shortlist candidates by hand. Separately, team leads try to spot disengagement through one-to-ones. We want a vendor's machine-learning tool to rank applicants and automatically reject those below a cut-off, and to score employee sentiment continuously from workplace chat messages so HR can flag low performers and disengaged staff for follow-up.

subtasks.name: Review incoming applications
subtasks.description: Recruiters read the several hundred applications received for each warehouse and driver posting to understand who has applied.
subtasks.rationale: Reading and sorting applications is routine and high in volume. Errors here are caught when candidates are shortlisted.

subtasks.name: Rank applicants with ML tool
subtasks.description: A vendor's machine-learning tool would score and rank applicants for each posting so that the best-fitting ones rise to the top.
subtasks.rationale: The ranking directly drives who is considered for hiring. Errors or bias would change outcomes for many applicants.

subtasks.name: Reject applicants below cut-off
subtasks.description: The tool would automatically reject applicants whose score falls below a set cut-off, with no person reviewing the result.
subtasks.rationale: An automatic rejection is a hiring decision affecting livelihood. The cut-off rule is simple but its effects are significant.

subtasks.name: Score employee sentiment from chat
subtasks.description: The tool would continuously analyze workplace chat messages and give each employee a sentiment score.
subtasks.rationale: Scores about identifiable staff feed HR follow-up. Errors could harm trust and employment standing, and the monitoring runs constantly.

subtasks.name: Flag low performers and disengaged staff
subtasks.description: HR uses the sentiment scores to flag employees seen as low performers or disengaged and to select them for follow-up.
subtasks.rationale: Flagging shapes how managers treat employees and may lead to performance management. A wrong flag can hurt livelihood and trust.

assumptions: The tool scores applicants using the content of their applications.
Rejected applicants are not reviewed by a person before being told.
Sentiment scores are linked to named employees, not only to teams.
HR relies on the scores when choosing whom to follow up with.
Employees may not be fully aware their chat messages are analyzed.
clarifyingQuestions: Does anyone review applicants rejected below the cut-off before they are notified?
Are sentiment scores shown for individual employees or only for teams?
What does follow-up involve for a flagged employee, and could it affect their performance record?
